meta.title: FEAT-004 · Google sign-in with auto-link
meta.subtitle: Design solution from technical-design.md: the components this slice changes, the contract on every arrow, and the decisions behind them. Pick a flow to follow one use-case path; click any arrow for its data contract.
meta.description: A visitor on the storefront sign-in page chooses Google. The browser navigates to Identity through the gateway, which redirects it to Google with code flow, PKCE, state and nonce. After consent Google redirects back to Identity's callback, where the OpenID Connect handler redeems the code and validates the ID token, then parks the Google principal in a short-lived hs.ext cookie. The complete endpoint decides: a known Google identity signs in, a verified email matching an account links to it (and for an unverified account removes its password and sessions), and no match creates a verified Buyer without a password. Identity starts the hs.idp session and writes ExternalLoginLinked to the outbox in the same transaction. Notification stores the contact and emails the owner only when an existing account was linked. If Google is down or invalid the visitor is sent back to the sign-in page with a stable error code and password sign-in keeps working.
overview: new table external_logins (unique provider+subject, unique user+provider)
meta.footnote: Source: docs/features/FEAT-004-google-sign-in/technical-design.md (§3 contracts, §5 components, §7 decisions, §8 open items). Generated with html-flow-diagram; edit design-flow.model.json and rebuild.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.desc: The visitor. Follows redirects between the storefront, Identity and Google. Holds hs.idp after sign-in and, briefly, hs.ext and the correlation and nonce cookies (SameSite Lax).

nodes.label: Storefront SPA
nodes.desc: SignInPage.vue: the Google button and divider, navigating to /connect/external/google/start?returnUrl=… (a full-page navigation, no fetch). Reads ?error= and shows the vi/en message for the four known codes; unknown values are ignored. The password form always stays usable.

nodes.label: Gateway + BFF
nodes.desc: Existing anonymous route /connect/{**rest} → identity. Strips only hs.bff* cookies, so Identity's correlation, nonce, hs.ext and hs.idp cookies pass in both directions. No CSRF header on GET.

nodes.label: Identity
nodes.desc: Api: provider registry, hs.ext cookie, OpenID Connect scheme google (code, PKCE S256, state, nonce, scope openid email profile), start and complete endpoints, ExternalFailure.Classify. Application: ExternalSignInHandler. Change: /connect/authorize now matches pwd_at exactly, also when the account has no credential.

nodes.label: identitydb
nodes.desc: New table external_logins (user_id, provider, subject, linked_at). A Google-created user has no credentials row; linking an unverified account deletes its row (D-5). OpenIddict tables get revoked for that account.

nodes.label: Service Bus
nodes.desc: Outbox relay, at least once. Carries ExternalLoginLinked/v1 to Notification.

nodes.label: Notification
nodes.desc: ExternalLoginLinked upserts the contact for every event, and sends template external_login_linked only when accountCreated is false (vi/en, Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh time, extra paragraph when passwordRemoved). Payload validated by a pydantic model mirroring the schema.

nodes.label: notificationdb
nodes.desc: No schema change. email_records unique on (event_id, template) keeps the notice idempotent.

nodes.label: Email provider
nodes.desc: SMTP (Mailpit locally). Sent after commit; failure is recorded as failed (retries are FEAT-032).

nodes.label: Google / fake IdP
nodes.desc: Google in the demo; tools/fake-idp in tests, the AppHost and E2E (a real OIDC server with discovery, JWKS, PKCE checks and a /__fake/next control endpoint). Selected by Identity:Google:Authority. Calls have a 5 s timeout.

all.title: FEAT-004 design solution
all.intro: Five paths: a new Google account, linking to an existing account, a denied or unverified response, Google unavailable, and the guards.

steps.t: start: Identity checks the provider and returnUrl and answers 302 to Google.
Consent at Google (code flow, PKCE S256, state, nonce, openid email profile).
callback: Identity redeems the code and validates the ID token; the Google principal waits in hs.ext.
complete: no account matches, so one transaction creates a verified Buyer with no password, the link and the outbox row; hs.idp starts.
Event stores the contact; no email is sent for a created account.
Same start; the verified Google email matches an account.

One transaction adds the link; the account keeps its password. When its email was unverified, the email is verified, the credential deleted, every session revoked and pending tokens invalidated (D-5).
Notice email to the owner in their language; a duplicate delivery sends once.
Consent denied, or the response carries email_verified: false, no email, a bad state, nonce or signature.
302 to /signin?error=… with external_login_denied, external_email_unverified or external_login_failed, returnUrl kept. No cookie, no account, no link.
start awaits Google's metadata for at most 5 s.
Metadata, token or JWKS call fails or times out.
302 to /signin?error=identity.external_login_unavailable; the page says Google is unavailable and the password form keeps working. Metadata is retried after 30 s.
Returning Google user is found by (provider, subject) first: no write, no event, even after a Google email change.
returnUrl is honored only as a local /connect/authorize… path; an unknown provider is 404; a replayed complete fails.
No password on the account: POST /v1/users/sign-in gives the same 401 as an unknown email; PUT /v1/me/password gives 409 identity.password_not_set (FEAT-003).

notes.t: OpenID Connect handler behind a registry
notes.b: The ASP.NET Core handler gives PKCE, state, nonce and ID-token validation; a second provider is one registration and a claim map. Rejected: the Google-only package and a hand-written client.
Identity sits behind the gateway, so the request host is internal. The fixed URI is set on both the authorize and the code-redeem request.

notes.t: Unverified account: drop password and sessions
notes.b: Closes pre-account-hijacking (an attacker registers the victim's email first). Goes beyond the SRS text "link and sign in": confirmed by the user (hybrid: delete and notify now, set a new password later in FEAT-005).

notes.t: One event for created and linked
notes.b: ExternalLoginLinked with accountCreated; UserRegistered would force a verification token and email. Notification mails only when an account was linked.

notes.t: Match by subject first, then email
notes.b: sub is the only stable Google id; a changed Google email must not re-link or detach.

notes.t: Errors are redirects with stable codes
notes.b: No JSON body in a redirect chain; the SPA localizes ?error= from its own vi/en keys.

notes.t: Fake IdP is a real OIDC server
notes.b: tools/fake-idp serves integration tests, the AppHost and E2E, so discovery, PKCE and signature checks are really exercised.

notes.t: No attempt limit or audit yet
notes.b: Rate limits, lockout and the sign-in audit log arrive with FEAT-005 (NFR-SEC-009).
FEAT-004 relies on its pwd_at stamp, ISessionRevoker and password_not_set. Merge it first.
FR-AUTH-020's note mentions the Google picture; there is no avatar until FEAT-035, so only the name is prefilled.
Needed only for a manual real-Google run; CI runs entirely on the fake IdP. Put the real client in .local/dev-secrets/google.json before the demo release.
